subject: Iterating multiple times over the same model and same data

messages.author: 7a0d46cfe7d661bf
messages.subject: Iterating multiple times over the same model and same data
parts:
I am trying to sample from my posterior distribution using PyStan. I need the results ASAP however I don't know the number of iterations needed. The code have been running for 4 hours now and I am only ran 15,000 iterations. 

I was wondering if it's possible to run the code, save the samples, and then run the code again till I reach convergence. 
To make it clearer, let's say the first time I run:

fit = pystan.stan(model_code=fit_code, data=fit_data, iter=15000, chains=4)

#save the samples

with open('samples.pkl', 'w') as f:

     pickle.dump(fit, f)


and then the second time I run:

# load the samples
with open('samples.pkl', 'r') as f:
    model = pickle.load(f)


# sample from the posterior
fit = pystan.stan(fit=model, data=fit_data, iter=15000, chains=4)


Is it equivalent to iterating 30,000 times? 
I tried it, however I got an error when loading the pickle file.

   vector[N] y; // y values

   y ~ normal(ytrue, yerr);

"""

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Iterating multiple times over the same model and same data
parts:
The default for theta is uniform, and because theta is a simplex,
that's proper.

375 data points is not many at all. You shouldn't need
15K iterations to get reasonable effective sample size.

- Bob

P.S. The model looks like a mixture model with measurement error for x
and then another measurement error model for y and a simple
regression of y on x. Not sure what that does all together.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Iterating multiple times over the same model and same data
parts:
No. Millions of parameters are a lot, or 100s of thousands
in some cases.

- Bob

> On May 15, 2015, at 2:10 AM, Paula Sarkis <paula.s...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
>
> On May 15, 2015 07:40, "Bob Carpenter" <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
> >
> > The default for theta is uniform, and because theta is a simplex,
> > that's proper.
>
> So I should put/fix a prior on theta.
>
> > 375 data points is not many at all. You shouldn't need
> > 15K iterations to get reasonable effective sample size.
> >
> I have 373 data points which is equivalent to having 755 parameters in my model to make inference on. (Xtrue (373) + ytrue (373) + alpha. Beta, sigma (3) + K=2 Gaussians (6) which sum up to 755 parameters).
>
> Now my question is 755 parameters considered a lot?

You'll have to quantify what you mean by a lot!

We've fit models with over a million parameters and millions
of data points, but have had more trouble (in terms of speed)
with models with a few thousand parameters and much more complex
structure.

> > P.S. The model looks like a mixture model with measurement error for x
> > and then another measurement error model for y and a simple
> > regression of y on x. Not sure what that does all together.
> >
>
> True! That's exactly what I'm trying to do. I'm trying to fit a straight line to my data points with measurement errors on both the dependent and independent parameters.
>
> I'm not next to the laptop now, but basically if I fix my priors should 15000 interactions with 4 chains be enough?

Depends on what you want to do. You want to look at n_eff, which
is the effective number of samples you have and the se column, which
estimate error on posterior mean estimates.

Usually a few hundred iterations run with four chains are plenty --- it
gets std errors well below posterior std deviation for parameters. 100
effective samples means std errors that are 10% of posterior std deviations.

- Bob

> >>   ytrue ~ normal(ymodel, sigma);
> >>
> >>   x ~ normal(xtrue, xerr);
> >>
> >>   y ~ normal(ytrue, yerr);
> >>
> >> }
> >>
> >> """

messages.author: 7a0d46cfe7d661bf
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Iterating multiple times over the same model and same data
parts:
On Fri, May 15, 2015 at 9:00 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
No.  Millions of parameters are a lot, or 100s of thousands
in some cases.

- Bob

> On May 15, 2015, at 2:10 AM, Paula Sarkis <paula.s...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
>
> On May 15, 2015 07:40, "Bob Carpenter" <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
> >
> > The default for theta is uniform, and because theta is a simplex,
> > that's proper.
>
> So I should put/fix a prior on theta.
>
> > 375 data points is not many at all.  You shouldn't need
> > 15K iterations to get reasonable effective sample size.
> >
> I have 373 data points which is equivalent to having 755 parameters in my model to make inference on. (Xtrue (373) + ytrue (373) + alpha. Beta, sigma (3) + K=2 Gaussians (6) which sum up to 755 parameters).
>
> Now my question is 755 parameters considered a lot?

You'll have to quantify what you mean by a lot!

We've fit models with over a million parameters and millions
of data points, but have had more trouble (in terms of speed)
with models with a few thousand parameters and much more complex
structure.

My main concern is that I want to make sure PyStan handles a large number of parameters. I was using the package emcee first, but I was told that the package does not handle more than 30 parameters. From your answer, I can safely assume that PyStan can handle ~ 750 parameters.

> > P.S.  The model looks like a mixture model with measurement error for x
> > and then another measurement error model for y and a simple
> > regression of y on x.   Not sure what that does all together.
> >
>
> True! That's exactly what I'm trying to do. I'm trying to fit a straight line to my data points with measurement errors on both the dependent and independent parameters.
>
> I'm not next to the laptop now, but basically if I fix my priors should 15000 interactions with 4 chains be enough?

Depends on what you want to do.  You want to look at n_eff, which
is the effective number of samples you have and the se column, which
estimate error on posterior mean estimates.

Usually a few hundred iterations run with four chains are plenty --- it
gets std errors well below posterior std deviation for parameters.  100
effective samples means std errors that are 10% of posterior std deviations.

I think my main problem is that the dependent parameters have very small error bars (on the order of 10^{-4} - 10^{-5}). Please correct me if I am wrong. The model did not converge with 15,000 iterations and 4 chains because of the small variances I have, right?
Is there a special way to handle small variances in the likelihood?

Thanks for your help,
Paula
 

- Bob

The ensemble methods can have a hard time with high
dimensionality, but HMC scales well with dimension and
Stan's relatively tight with memory so you should be OK.

- Bob
